name: Samoa

findings.controller: Alcatel Submarine Networks (ASN, France; then part of Nokia)
findings.local_actor: Samoa Submarine Cable Company Ltd (SSCC, private, Apia)
findings.summary: The Tui-Samoa cable, over 1,470 km from Apia to Suva with spurs to Savai'i and Wallis and Futuna, was supplied turnkey by ASN under a 2016 contract with SSCC and was reported live in May 2018.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment-vendor rule: ASN (French) supplied the cable, so pole third; owner-operator SSCC is domestic. Contract value and financier not stated in opened sources. Pre-2020; in-service status as of 2026 not reconfirmed, so still_current null.

findings.summary: Bluesky announced a partnership with Huawei to upgrade its Samoa 2G/3G network to 4.5G LTE-Advanced, including WTTx fixed-wireless broadband and VoLTE, covering Samoa, American Samoa and the Cook Islands.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 5 because a later undated Samoa Observer report states Huawei provides 4G/4.5G technology across Samoa for Bluesky and Digicel; both opened sources share one host, so not corroborated. Whether Vodafone Samoa's 2024 5G uses Huawei is unknown (launch report names no vendor). Pre-2020, still_current null.

findings.local_actor: Digicel Samoa (Digicel Pacific, owned by Telstra since 2022)
findings.summary: Telstra said it would keep the Huawei equipment running Digicel Pacific's 3G/4G networks, including Samoa, after its 2022 acquisition, without near-term upgrades, aligning with Australian standards only at future refreshes.
findings.analyst_inference: Samoa is named only in a list of Digicel markets relying on Huawei gear; the Samoa Observer piece independently says Digicel works with Huawei for 4G. No S1/S2 source opened. Nokia 5G overlay (WSM-004) may signal the refresh Telstra described, but no Huawei removal is reported, so no reversal coded.

findings.summary: After conditional government approval in March 2024, Digicel Samoa upgraded sites with Nokia AirScale non-standalone 5G and switched on Samoa's first live 5G at five sites in Apia's central business district in July 2024.
findings.analyst_inference: Nokia (Finland) supplies the 5G radio, so pole third. NSA 5G rides on the existing 4G core/RAN, which per WSM-003 was Huawei; mixed-vendor network inferred. Go-live date from 'Monday' before 9 July 2024 article. Scale municipal: five Apia sites only.

findings.local_actor: Samoa Police Service; Australian Federal Police (technical partner)
findings.summary: Samoa Police and the Australian Federal Police launched an Australian-funded Safer CCTV Network of 30 cameras with a monitoring room and emergency radio network, part of a roughly AUD 6.5m three-year investment ahead of CHOGM 2024.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: equipment vendor, which sets the pole under the equipment rule, is not named. Australian financing does not set pole. AUD 6.5m covers a wider policing package, so not recorded as a value. Partial launch; full operation was due before October 2024.

findings.controller: Government of Samoa (Ministry of Communications and Information Technology)
findings.local_actor: MCIT; Office of the Regulator; Ministry of Finance (executing agency)
findings.summary: The World Bank-financed Digitally Connected and Resilient Samoa project includes upgrading and establishing a secure, resilient government data centre alongside a national fibre network and government intranet upgrades.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology, Samoa

findings.analyst_inference: Owner-operator rule: government-run data centre, so domestic; World Bank is financier only. Tier 2 because the page describes a planned component with no award, construction or completion; project value and dates not stated (linked documents appear to be 2024). No vendors named.

silicon.null_reason: no dedicated search; no accelerator purchase or deployment surfaced in facilities, models or network searches

models.null_reason: one search found only UNDP AI-readiness work and an April 2026 MCIT speech at the World Internet Conference (Hong Kong) with no agreement; no frontier-provider partnership or sovereign model found

research_gaps: Vodafone Samoa (ATH-owned) 5G vendor for its September 2024 soft launch at 11 CHOGM sites; launch report names none. Is it still Huawei as for Bluesky's 4.5G?
Whether Digicel Samoa's Nokia 5G upgrade replaced any Huawei RAN/core (a possible commercial or geopolitical swap) or is an overlay only.
Safer CCTV Network camera and VMS vendor; check Australian procurement (AusTender) records.
Digital Samoa project: World Bank approval date, financing amount, and whether the government data centre has been tendered or awarded and to whom.
Samoa's second cable links (e.g. Manatua, SAS) and their suppliers; whether any HMN Tech involvement exists.
AidData lists PRC-financed Samoa projects (only one opened, a 2007 vehicle donation); check for ICT, e-government or police-surveillance items.
